Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size reservoir of randomly connected nodes, which transform input data into a high-dimensional space. Training in ESNs is typically done by adjusting the output weights only, while the reservoir itself is usually not trained but kept fixed. This approach simplifies the training process and can be more efficient for certain tasks.
